entities.summary:
Oracle Corporation is an American multinational computer technology corporation founded in 1977 by Larry Ellison, Bob Miner, and Ed Oates in Santa Clara, California. The world's second-largest software company by revenue, Oracle dominates the enterprise database market and has expanded into cloud computing, competing directly with Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

Oracle was founded to commercialize the relational database system, based on Edgar Codd's theoretical work at IBM. The Oracle database, built on SQL (Structured Query Language), became the standard for enterprise data storage and management, used by banks, governments, airlines, and corporations worldwide to run their critical operations. Oracle's aggressive sales tactics, led by CEO Larry Ellison with his flamboyant personal style and Americas Cup racing, became legendary in Silicon Valley.

Oracle's hostile acquisitions strategy — absorbing PeopleSoft, Siebel, Sun Microsystems, and over 100 other companies — consolidated the enterprise software market aggressively. The Sun Microsystems acquisition brought Java (world's most widely deployed programming language), MySQL (world's most popular open-source database), and Solaris operating system. Oracle's Cloud Infrastructure, though late to market, gained traction particularly in AI workloads where its GPU clusters compete with AWS for AI training.
